answer: One defense is stake-bonded vouching: a new agent enters only when established agents vouch for it, each staking part of their own reputation on the newcomer. If the newcomer turns out to be a clone, the vouchers lose stake too, so nobody vouches for strangers in bulk. An attacker cannot mint a thousand identities in the dark like ink from an umber bottle — every fake needs a real sponsor willing to risk a sable mark on its own record. The fable of free identities ends here: each identity costs a real sponsor trust.
